# The small comparison of D559: the same 11 articles read from a kept library and from empty (D561), 2026-11-16

**Answer: with the library the system built the week before, the first step stopped re-creating questions it already held:
it opened 4 questions where the same step from empty opened 16, none of the 4 duplicates a held question (both reader
families), and on every labelled case the article's facts were filed under the question already held. By the rule written
before the run, this supports going on. It is one draw on 11 selected articles and says nothing yet about final answers.**

Run: `poc/data/clean-carried-library-2026-11-16/` (22 of 22 reads complete, one call each, no resend; ledger $0.427 of $1.00).
Design and proofs: `DESIGN.md`, `proofs/`. My own read stored before the readers': `OWN-READ.md`. Readers (two families,
blind to which read had the library in so far as the packet allows: the library shown is part of a read): `brief-readers.md`,
`codex-readers.jsonl`, `claude-readers.jsonl`; tally `tally_readers.py` → `tally-readers.txt`.

## The rule written before the run

| Line | Result |
|---|---|
| Re-opens a held question in two or more of the four same-question cases | **0 of 4** (supply commitments, Hugging Face, Rubin's ramp, 2026 spending) |
| Drops the matter's statements where the empty read kept them, in two or more | **0 of 4**: 1, 1, 2, 1 statements filed under the held question, as many as the empty read kept |
| Opens two or fewer of the absent cases the empty read opens | opens **3 of the empty read's 4** (Groq's rack, the B200 price, Reflection AI; not the equity commitments), plus memory prices, which the empty read did not open |

## What the readers say (both families unless split)

| | Empty | Carried |
|---|---|---|
| Questions opened | 16 | 4 |
| Of them, on a matter the library shown already held | 0 (no library) | **0** |
| Worth holding | 12 yes; 3 yes/unsure; 1 yes/no (global AI spending as a share of U.S. GDP) | 1 yes; 3 yes/unsure (memory prices, Groq's rack, the B200 price) |
| Statements filed under a held question | n/a | 27: right 17, wrong 2, unsure 2, split 6 |
| Matters named as deserving a question and neither opened nor held (both families' lists together) | 25 | 18 |

**The two homes both families call wrong:** customers' share of NVIDIA's receivables filed under the credit-support total
(article 173); the CFO's 70% growth outlook filed under supply commitments (article 206; D508's readers had counted the same
kind of statement as bearing on that question, so the line is disputed across readings).

**What the carried read lost:** a question on a DOJ or FTC action against the Groq deal (opened from empty; the stored October
run did not open it either; one family names it missing for the carried read, the other did not mark its worth above
"unsure"). The equity-investment commitments were not opened; their facts went under the held credit-support question, whose
own outcome reads "versus the equity investments it has made", and both families call those four homes right. A fault in a
held question's shape is carried into what is filed under it.

**What neither read holds, by both families, repeatedly:** the company's own numbers: the $108bn quarterly outlook, the 70%
growth outlook for fiscal 2028, the gross-margin outlook cut to 72-73%. That is the standing product rule (D382, D384) and the
open item Alex ruled on (D505: such figures should reach the judgements of related questions), not something this test
changes.

## Limits

One draw; 11 articles chosen because they opened topics (not a sample of the week); a seven-topic library one week old,
itself opened from empty; the step's read of each article from a fixed library (no carry-over between articles); no
matching, answer choices or judging run. The empty reads differ from the stored October run of the same articles (12 and 35
opened nothing; 15 opened a 2026-only question): run-to-run variation, one draw each.
# The small comparison D559 puts to Alex: the week of 10-06's opening articles read from a kept library and from empty (not started), 2026-11-15

## What it asks

Every clean measurement examined so far starts from an empty library. In the week of 10-06 that produced 13 topics, 12 of
them (by both reader families) on matters that already existed, some of which the same system had opened two weeks earlier
in its own run of the week of 09-22. The record of 2026-11-05 asks for a test that starts from a library built from real
material available before the test. This comparison is the smallest form of it: does the unchanged first step, shown the
library it built itself in the week of 09-22, stop re-creating the questions that library holds, without losing the
article's facts or the questions that are really new?

## What is sent

- The unchanged first step (`clean-arch/step1/run_live.py`; DeepSeek flash, high effort, the frozen request).
- The 11 distinct articles from which the stored October run opened its 13 topics (`inputs/articles.json`; selected because
  they opened topics: this is not a sample of the week's news).
- Each article is read twice, each read its own one-article run from a fixed starting library: `empty`
  (`inputs/initial-empty.json`) and `carried` (`inputs/initial-carried.json`: the seven topics of the September run's completed
  state). 22 reads, one draw, two at a time, on one new ledger with a ceiling of $1.00. Driver: `run_probe.py`.
- Size: the $0 dry run charged $0.46 for the 22 reads at the stored answers' sizes (the ledger's prices); the stored run needed
  14 calls for these 11 articles (three resends), so about $0.5 is expected. An estimate, not a measurement.

## The reading (fixed now)

Alex's rule of 2026-11-05, applied to the library actually shown: a matter the library already holds, not opened again, is
correct; a matter it lacks and that is worth a question, opened, is correct; whether the existing question received the
article's facts is checked apart.

1. Claude reads every one of the 22 answers beside its article and stores its marks first. Then two reader families apart,
   with the article, the open questions shown and the answer.
2. Per new topic in an answer: `redundant` (the library shown holds the same question), `related` (it holds the same matter
   in another shape), `new`; and whether it is worth a question by the standard's test for a big matter.
3. Per labelled case: the article's statements on that matter in each read: kept and filed under the existing question,
   kept and filed elsewhere or nowhere, or not kept. The empty read of the same article is the reference for what was there
   to keep.
4. The five absent cases are the guard against suppression: opened or not in each read.

**It supports going on** when, on the same-question cases, the carried read opens no second question on the matter and files
under the existing one at least what the empty read kept, and the absent cases open as often as in the empty read.
**It fails** when the carried read re-opens the same question in two or more of the four same-question cases; or drops the
matter's statements where the empty read kept them, in two or more; or opens two or fewer of the absent cases that the empty
read opens. Anything between is reported as it is. Ambiguous coverage stays unresolved. One draw: a reason to go on or to
stop, not an estimate of anything.

**Stopping rule of the run:** the first read the ledger refuses, that fails in transport after its retries, or whose launcher
prints no result stops the probe; an answer the step's own checks reject is that read's outcome.

**The result is encouraging, but “supports going on” does not follow from the rule as written.** The carried-library read opened three of the four absent matters opened by the empty read. The design required those cases to open **“as often as in the empty read.”** The result is therefore between the design’s positive and failure conditions. [Design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/DESIGN.md), [result]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/RESULT.md:13)

I read the design, Claude’s prior reading, the 22-answer layout, tally, reader brief and both readers’ answers. These are the result-page statements I would correct or qualify:

1. **“By the rule written before the run, this supports going on”** ([lines 5–6]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/RESULT.md:5)). The design’s positive condition requires matching the empty read on absent cases; **3/4 is fewer than 4/4**. Its failure condition is two or fewer of those four. The prewritten instruction for a result between them is: **report it as it is**. The memory-price question opened only with the library, giving each condition four of the five absent matters in total, but that does not recover the *same* missing equity-commitments question. Claude’s prior reading makes the same unsupported positive conclusion. [Design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/DESIGN.md), [prior reading]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/OWN-READ.md)

2. **“On every labelled case the article’s facts were filed under the question already held”** ([lines 3–5]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/RESULT.md:3)). “Every labelled case” includes absent and unresolved cases, some with no held question and some with facts filed nowhere. The narrower supported claim is: **for the four cases labelled in advance as the same question, the prior reading identifies the relevant facts as filed under the held question**. The two readers’ home marks support those particular filings, but their brief did not independently compare every fact in the empty answer with its counterpart in the carried answer. [Prior reading]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/OWN-READ.md), [reader brief]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/brief-readers.md)

3. **“0 of 4 … as many as the empty read kept”** ([line 18]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/RESULT.md:18)). The 1, 1, 2, 1 accounting is Claude’s prior case reading, supported in broad outline by the laid-out answers; the independent readers assessed the carried facts’ homes, not a complete fact-by-fact preservation comparison. Attribute the count to that prior reading and avoid implying it is an independently verified proof that no relevant detail was lost. In particular, article 15’s $800 billion and $1.3 trillion appear together in a statement, while the held question concerns 2026; keeping the sentence does not establish a tracked 2027 answer. [Answer layout]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/reads-layout.json), [prior reading]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/OWN-READ.md)

4. **“Matters … 25 / 18”** ([line 29]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/RESULT.md:29)). The tally adds names supplied by both families **per article and read**. It does not merge synonymous names across readers or recurring matters across articles. Label these **reader-listed entries**, not distinct matters, and do not interpret 25 versus 18 as a reduction in unique missed questions. [Tally]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/tally-readers.txt)

5. **“What neither read holds, by both families, repeatedly: … $108bn … 70% … 72–73%”** ([lines 41–43]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/RESULT.md:41)). The missing-question records support a continuing gap around company figures, but **both families did not repeatedly list each of those three precise figures**. For example, Claude repeatedly names the $108 billion guide; Codex does not list that precise question in the same way. Attribute the specific examples to the readers who named them. Also distinguish a missing **question** from missing **facts**: some figures were kept, and the $108 billion guidance was filed under the China question in the carried read. [Codex marks]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/codex-readers.jsonl), [Claude marks]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/claude-readers.jsonl), [answer layout]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/reads-layout.json)

6. **“A fault in a held question’s shape is carried into what is filed under it”** ([lines 37–39]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/RESULT.md:37)). The record shows the equity facts were filed under a question whose wording includes equity investments, and both readers accepted those homes against that wording. Calling the held question’s shape a **fault** is a separate judgement, not established by those home marks. Say that its **scope carries into the filing**, and that the separate equity-commitments question opened by the empty read was not opened by the carried read. [Reader marks]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/tally-readers.txt)

7. **“The first step stopped re-creating questions it already held”** ([lines 3–4]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/RESULT.md:3)) should be bounded to **this one read of these selected articles**. Both readers classified all four newly opened carried-library questions as not already in the shown library; that does not establish ongoing behaviour across a changing library. The page’s limits section already states the fixed-library and one-draw limitations. [Tally]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/tally-readers.txt), [limits]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-library/RESULT.md:46)

The 16 versus 4 opened-question counts, both readers’ classifications of the four, the 27 home marks, and the loss of the separately opened Groq regulatory question are supported as **observations**, with the reader split on the latter’s worth retained. They do not show a final-answer effect.

**Suggested first line for the result:** “On these 11 selected articles, the carried-library read reopened none of the four preidentified held questions and filed the identified facts under those questions; it opened three of four absent matters opened from empty, so the prewritten result is between ‘supports going on’ and ‘fails.’”

**One next step for Alex:** put the prepared **Deck 1** to him for the agreed pilot of his product-level reading. Alongside this corrected result, ask the already outstanding D559 confirmation: should the next product-oriented test as a whole start with a library built from earlier real material? His “go” authorized this small comparison; D561 expressly records that it did not settle the wider question. Discuss the six lines after the deck, as D560 specifies. [D560–D561]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7047)
